Naomi Oreskes is a renowned historian of science and professor at Harvard University, known for her groundbreaking work on the role of science in society and the defense of scientific integrity. Her research focuses on the history of climate science, scientific consensus, and the ways industries have challenged scientific evidence in the public sphere.
She is the co-author (with Erik Conway) of the bestselling book Merchants of Doubt, which exposes how a small group of scientists obscured the truth on issues ranging from tobacco smoke to climate change. She is also the author or co-author of eight other titles, including the award-winning Science on a Mission: How Military Funding Shaped What We Do and Don't Know about the Ocean. Her work has been translated into multiple languages and adapted into an award-winning documentary film.
